root_idea.summary: The root denotes speed and quickness, in opposition to slowness.
root_idea.development: Its semantic range develops from rapid movement or action to hastening toward a goal, striving to get ahead, precedence, and idioms expressing exceptional immediacy.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form III perfect citation form سَارَعَ.
Displayed as the elative adjective أَسْرَعُ.
Displayed under the adjective citation form سَرِيعٌ.
Displayed as the Quran-attested verbal-noun form سِرَاعٌ.

senses.definition: To hasten toward or into something; to make haste to reach or undertake it.
senses.usage_conditions: With إِلَى, the construction expresses hastening toward a goal. With فِي, it can express rushing into a course or condition, including good works, unbelief, or wrongdoing.

senses.definition: To vie with another or others in hastening, striving to arrive first or get ahead.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the competitive or reciprocal use of Form III; the goal of the striving may be expressed with إِلَى.
The Quranic form occurs in predicates describing the speed or promptness of an action, especially in expressions concerning reckoning and punishment.

senses.definition: Prompt and not delayed in reckoning or punishment.
senses.usage_conditions: In the predicates سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ and سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ, the adjective conveys the immediate and inevitable execution of divine reckoning or punishment, rather than physical speed.
This elative adjective expresses comparison or superlative degree; in the Quran it is used of the one quickest in reckoning and of something more swift in response or outcome.

senses.definition: Hastening; rapid movement, used adverbially as “swiftly” or “rapidly.”
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences are accusative adverbial expressions describing coming forth or emerging with haste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be quick, expeditious, hasty, speedy, rapid, swift, or fleet; to be quick in speech or action, or for an affair or event to occur quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression سَرُعَ مَا فَعَلْتَ and its contracted forms can be an exclamation meaning “how quickly you did that!” or expressing remarkable quickness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To quicken or hasten oneself, one's pace, movement, or going; to make haste or speed; to hasten to a person, thing, or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be used elliptically or with a particle. أَسْرَعَ بِالأَمْرِ means to hasten to carry out an affair; of riding beasts, أَسْرَعُوا means that they became swift. In a reported idiom, أَسْرَعَ إِلَيْهِ can mean being quick in anger, blame, or reviling toward him. The exclamation مَا أَسْرَعَ مَا صَنَعْتَ means “how quickly you did that!”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quickness, speed, rapidity, or haste; the act or state of hastening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe the speed of a course, tendency, action, speech, or other occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An idiomatic exclamation of sudden or remarkable quickness: “how quickly ...!”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It occurs especially in expressions such as سَرْعَانَ مَا followed by an event or action, and has dialectal variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foremost people or horsemen, those striving with one another to be first to do or reach something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is applied to people or horsemen who are at the front through their haste or competitive precedence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swift ones or those hastening; a plural of سَرِيعٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same plural sense is also expressed by سُرْعَانٌ in Classical Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick or prompt to do good or evil, or quick in affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical Arabic specialization describing an agent's readiness or speed in undertaking an action, rather than the Quranic divine predicates of reckoning or punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular kind of gait or pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical usage occurring in a collocation with سُنْبُكٌ, which denotes another kind of pace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The ninth metre of Arabic prosody.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a technical prosodic designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The plant called عَرْفَج, or the fire contained in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a lexicalized plant or fire-name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shoot or twig that falls from the بشام tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its reported plurals include سِرْعَانٌ and سُرْعَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very quick or hasty, especially one quick to do good or evil or quick in affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intensive descriptive form applied to a person or other subject characterized by exceptional haste.

The Quranic سِرَاعٌ group is classified in the supplied QAC morphology as a verbal noun, while Classical evidence also attests سِرَاعٌ as a plural of سَرِيعٌ; these uses are kept distinct.
